name: Karirí-Xocó
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: Usamos de dous accentos, hum agudo, & outro circumflexo. O agudo serve para carregar sobre a vogal, v. g. Sambé, paga. Ordinariamente se acha na derradeira vogal de todos os vocabulos desta lingua, excepto algũas palavras que náo acabaõ em agudo, como Bæ, De, & alguns poucos vocabulos, que a experiencia ensinará. Sobre o til não se poem accento agudo, para evitar a confusaõ na escritura; mas basta advertir que o til sempre he agudo. ... E havendo outros accentos agudos na mesma dicção, he sinal q̃ he composta, & cada huma das partes fica na composiçam com o seu accento agudo: v.g. Tçohóhehéde, estaõ alguns poucos.
new_statements.translation: We use two accents, an acute and a circumflex. The acute serves to bear down on [stress] the vowel, e.g. Sambé 'pay'. Ordinarily it is found on the last vowel of all the words of this language, except some words that do not end in an acute, such as Bæ, De, and a few other words which experience will teach. No acute is written over the tilde, to avoid confusion in writing; but it suffices to note that the tilde [vowel] is always acute [stressed]. ... And when there are further acute accents in the same word, it is a sign that it is a compound, and each of the parts stays in the compound with its own acute accent: e.g. Tçohóhehéde 'there are a few'.
new_statements.citation: Mamiani, Luis Vincencio. 1699. Arte de grammatica da lingua brasilica da naçam Kiriri. Lisboa: Miguel Deslandes. [2a ed. Rio de Janeiro: Bibliotheca Nacional, 1877, same passage p. 4]
new_statements.locator: Parte I, §I 'Da orthographia, & pronunciação', 1699 ed. p. 5 (archive.org artedegrammatica00mami leaf n24); = 1877 ed. p. 4 (PDF p. 93 of artedegrammatic02rovegoog; render saved)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress (marked by the acute) falls on the final vowel of the word as the ordinary rule; a small set of words (Bæ, De and 'a few others') are lexical exceptions; nasal (tilde) vowels are always stressed; in compounds each member keeps its own stress, so a word with two acutes is a compound.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not described as such; compounds retain one stress per member (multiple acutes = compound).
new_statements.exceptions: 'algũas palavras que náo acabaõ em agudo, como Bæ, De, & alguns poucos vocabulos, que a experiencia ensinará'; final unaccented A/Æ (no acute, no tilde) is pronounced reduced 'como E Francez no fim da palavra' (e.g. Pide 'está', Tekiébæ 'não veyo').
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level orthoepic rule from a 1699 missionary ear-witness grammar of KIPEÁ Kiriri (Bahia), stated over citation/orthographic forms; not a description of the Alagoas Kariri-Xocó community's lost language. Queiroz 2008 p. 89 concurs second-hand ('Kipeá predominantemente oxítono').
new_statements.identity_note: kari1255 'Karirí-Xocó' (ISO kzw) is an ethnonym-based entry with no linguistic corpus of its own: the Porto Real do Colégio (AL) community had shifted to Portuguese before any description (Trujillo Ferrari 1956; Kroeker 1961 in Meader 1978 got 24 remembered words, partly Fulniô, filed under 'Xukurú-Karirí'). Glottolog 5.3 lists it as Unclassifiable with only Kipeá/Kariri-family refs attached, and the Glottolog GitHub master has already moved it to book1242 Bookkeeping. The statement quoted (Mamiani 1699 p. 5 = 1877 p. 4) describes KIPEÁ Kiriri = Glottolog kipe1235, a dialect under Kariri kari1254, which is ALREADY in the catalog (keyed kari1254, named 'Dzubukuá', source Queiroz 2012, reading lexical). The community's revived 'Kariri-Xocó (Dzubukuá Kipeá)' language (Kariri-Xocó et al. 2020) is likewise Kariri kari1254. Recommendation: do not create a kari1255 catalog entity (would double-count Kariri); if the Mamiani final-stress statement is wanted, key it to kipe1235 (Kipeá) as a dialect-level record alongside the Dzubukuá (dzub1241) record, as the kari1254 audit note already proposed.

sources.note: §I 'Da orthographia, & pronunciação', p. 5: the acute accent marks stress and 'Ordinariamente se acha na derradeira vogal de todos os vocabulos desta lingua', except a few words (Bæ, De and 'alguns poucos vocabulos'); final unaccented A/Æ is reduced like French final e; a word with more than one acute is a compound, each member keeping its own stress. Describes KIPEÁ Kiriri (kipe1235), not the Alagoas Kariri-Xocó.
No stress features (14A-17A) coded; sources Adam 1897, Larsen 1984, Rodrigues 1999b. Linked by Glottolog to kari1255 although it is Kipeá.

sources.citation: Queiroz, José Márcio Correia de. 2008. Aspectos da fonologia Dzubukuá. Dissertação (Mestrado em Letras), Universidade Federal de Pernambuco, Recife.
sources.note: About Dzubukuá (dzub1241), not Kariri-Xocó: p. 37 notes Trujillo Ferrari (1957) found the Kariri group near Porto Real do Colégio 'já não falava sua língua nativa, apenas o português'; p. 89 calls Kipeá 'predominantemente oxítono' (used as tie-breaker for Dzubukuá accent), Dzubukuá itself mostly paroxytone with oxytones and proparoxytones.

sources.citation: Mamiani, Luiz Vincencio. 1877 [1699]. Arte de grammatica da lingua brazilica da nação Kiriri. 2a edição. Rio de Janeiro: Bibliotheca Nacional (Typ. Central de Brown & Evaristo). (archive.org artedegrammatic02rovegoog, Google scan; p. 4 = PDF p. 93, rendered and read)
sources.note: Same passage in modernised spelling, printed p. 4: 'Ordinariamente se acha na derradeira vogal de todos os vocabulos desta lingua, excepto algũas palavras que não acabão em agudo, como Bæ, De, & alguns poucos vocabulos... E havendo outros accentos agudos na mesma dicção, he sinal que he composta, & cada huma das partes fica na composiçam com o seu accento agudo'.

Nothing. No classification comment; AES dormant (E29); the three refs attached (Mamiani 1877, Mamiani 1942 Catecismo, Queixalós 2003) are all Kipeá/Kariri-family works, MED-tagged 'wordlist_or_less' for this languoid; links WALS 'Kipea'.
Nothing on stress; identity evidence: in the current master the languoid has been moved under book1242 = Bookkeeping (spurious/duplicate ISO entry).

sources.citation: Kariri-Xocó, Idiane; Kariri-Xocó, Nhenety; Nelson, Diane; Pitman, Thea. 2020. A retomada da língua Kariri-Xocó. Cadernos de Linguística 1(3): 1-13. doi:10.25189/2675-4916.2020.v1.n3.id254
sources.note: Silent on stress. Revitalization report: 'A língua Kariri-Xocó (também conhecida como Dzubukuá Kipeá) pertence à família Kariri'; new lexicon coined from Kariri, Dzubukuá, Natú, Tupi; orthography note p. 10 (dz, ts; w = /u/, y = /i/); defers to Queiroz 2012 for grammar.

sources.citation: Meader, Robert E. (ed.). 1978. Índios do Nordeste: levantamento sobre os remanescentes tribais do Nordeste brasileiro. (Série Lingüística 8.) Brasília: Summer Institute of Linguistics. 94 pp.
sources.note: Nothing in prose. Sec. 1.12.1 'Porto Real do Colégio, AL' p. 20 (Kroeker 1961, the community today called Kariri-Xocó, then filed as Xukurú-Karirí): no speaker found; the Pajé 'Forneceu 24 palavras ao todo, e algumas delas podem ser Fulniô.' Sec. 3.10 Lista 1 p. 57 gives those 24 words in phonetic transcription with a stress stroke per token (b'áze, kràsut'ó, d'ódsáká, simid'o, kr'azo...). Intro pp. 8-9: many items Fulniô loans; 'a língua aqui designada como sendo Karirí é uma outra língua completamente diferente da que Mamiani estudou.'
